title: Jacket potatoes with split peas and red cabbage slaw

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, dried split peas, spices, cabbage, apple and lemon are all plain cupboard and garden foods.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including yellow split peas, is an everyday item at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking tray, one pan and a grater, and every technique is simple.

works.reason: 200g split peas in 900ml water makes a thick dhal-style filling for four, half a cabbage with an apple gives plenty of slaw, and 200°C for an hour suits baking potatoes.

honest_times.reason: Chopping an onion, shredding half a cabbage and grating an apple fit in 25 minutes, and the 45-minute simmer runs inside the 60-minute bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A crunchy red cabbage and apple slaw on a warm jacket potato suits mid-September, and half a cabbage makes it a main part of the plate rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear, British and free of restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Jacket potatoes with a spiced pulse filling and a fresh slaw make a filling, wholesome lunch a family would happily eat.
